title: Legal + FinOps: SSO, KMS, Pricing Decision Workshop
next_steps: Jordan to share redwood MSA + DPA annotated PDF by 2025-04-11
Priya to run a 24-hour perf benchmark on the customer's prompt set and share results by 2025-04-18
Customer to confirm preferred KMS flow (customer-managed vs Redwood) by 2025-04-15
action_items: Priya: perf benchmark (latency/cost) with 5k sample prompts, due 2025-04-18
Diego: provide network topology and egress constraints, due 2025-04-14
Renee: confirm procurement timeline and PO requirements, due 2025-04-16
summary: Working session between Redwood AE/SE and Helios Security/FinOps/Procurement to align on SSO, KMS ownership, SLA expectations, pricing buckets and procurement timeline. Key open items: MSA redlines, KMS integration approach, perf benchmark and egress costs. Agreed next steps and owners.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan Metz: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. sound check?
[00:00:08] Alex Rivera: hi Jordan, alex here. audio is good.
[00:00:11] Maya Chen: maya from finops, yep good.
[00:00:15] Priya Shah: priya (redwood SE) on the line, excited to dig into the KMS and perf asks.
[00:00:20] Jordan Metz: cool, agenda for 60 minutes, walk through MSA/DPA redlines, KMS options, SSO and RBAC, then pricing buckets and procurement path.
[00:00:34] Alex Rivera: quick ask up front — we need to confirm customer-managed KMS, and that keys never leave our HSM. is that supported?
[00:00:42] Priya Shah: we support customer-managed keys via integrated KMS/HSM in Redwood Private; for hosted there's a bring-your-own-key option but with slightly different egress patterns. i'll put the caveat in the slide deck.
[00:00:55] Diego Alvarez: when you say egress patterns, are you talking about tokenization of logs or actual crypto material leaving the HSM?
[00:01:02] Priya Shah: good q. crypto material never leaves HSM, but metadata and encrypted ciphertext can be routed; if you require total air-gap we typically recommend Private deployment in your VPC.
[00:01:16] Maya Chen: from FinOps perspective, we need transparency on token counts and egress fees, and ideally a pricing bucket for spikes.
[00:01:24] Jordan Metz: noted. we'll show our pricing tiers and an example billing calc against your sample traffic.
[00:01:31] Renee Park: procurement timeline: if legal signs off by week of 14th, we can cut PO the following week — but we need final pricing and any holdbacks clarified.
[00:01:40] Jordan Metz: understood. let's jump to the MSA redlines. Priya, can you summarize the typical exceptions enterprise customers request?
[00:01:48] Priya Shah: yes. common ones: SSO/SAML requirements, audit log retention, data residency, liability caps, and KMS control. also some orgs want stronger SLA windows — 99.99 vs 99.9.
[00:01:59] Alex Rivera: liability cap is one thing, but we really care about auditability — full request/response logging for a 12 month window and tamper-evident logs. is that something you provide?
[00:02:09] Priya Shah: we provide audit logs, can retain for configurable windows. tamper-evident storage is supported via write-once logs and integration with your SIEM. we'll attach our audit log spec.
[00:02:20] Jordan Metz: i'll include the security whitepaper link: https://redwood.example.com/security/audit-logs (note: placeholder link).
[00:02:27] Maya Chen: another question — for pricing, do you have a way to cap monthly spend or notify us when we hit thresholds?
[00:02:34] Jordan Metz: yes, console has budget alerts and token-level caps. for Dedicated we can set contractual burst limits and for hosted we have quota enforcement.
[00:02:42] Diego Alvarez: technical: how do you handle KV cache and state if we run in private vs hosted? we worry about cold-start latencies.
[00:02:51] Priya Shah: private deployment places KV cache in your VPC, so warmup is under your control; hosted uses a managed cache with warm pools but depending on traffic patterns cold starts can add overhead. we can propose config with pre-warm instances for your expected QPS.
[00:03:04] Alex Rivera: what about SOC 2/ISO stuff? we need level of compliance for our procurement pack.
[00:03:09] Jordan Metz: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and maintains ISO27001; we'll send the certs and our compliance pack.
[00:03:16] Renee Park: can you confirm data residency options? we need EU-only for certain cohorts.
[00:03:21] Priya Shah: yes, regional deployment options exist; for EU-only we can provision region-specific clusters and contractually restrict data flows. this sometimes ties into KMS location requirements.
[00:03:33] Maya Chen: back to pricing: what is the delta between hosted and dedicated per token?
[00:03:38] Jordan Metz: approximate: hosted is generally higher per-token but no infra commit; dedicated lowers unit cost by 30-60% depending on commit size. i'll share a sample model.
[00:03:48] Maya Chen: does the committed spend include egress fees?
[00:03:51] Jordan Metz: typically no — egress and KMS usage can be itemized separately. but we can roll egress into a committed arrangement if you want a blended rate.
[00:03:59] Diego Alvarez: for pilot we probably want hosted to move faster, but we need customer-managed keys for regulated data — is that compatible?
[00:04:07] Priya Shah: it's a common ask. we can do hosted with BYOK where the key is in your KMS and Redwood requests wrap/unwrap ops, but there's more coordination and slightly higher latency for each crypto op. we can show benchmark numbers.
[00:04:20] Jordan Metz: ok let's park that and go into the perf ask — Maya, you sent a sample set?
[00:04:25] Maya Chen: yes sent 5k anonymized prompts, mix of production and experimental. we want 95th percentile latency under 400ms for short prompts and cost per 1k tokens under $0.50 for pilot.
[00:04:36] Priya Shah: 95th p95 under 400ms is ambitious on shared hosted, but doable with dedicated and pre-warmed pools. for cost target we'll show quantization and batch config options to hit close to $0.50.
[00:04:48] Alex Rivera: i want to highlight security tradeoff — lowering cost by aggressive batching can increase data exposure windows and slightly raise risk profile.
[00:04:56] Priya Shah: yes, there's a tradeoff. we can enforce tenant-level isolation and per-request encryption. batching doesn't expose cross-tenant data, it's mostly timing.
[00:05:05] Jordan Metz: action: Priya will run perf with both hosted BYOK and Dedicated in-tenant using your prompt set.
[00:05:10] Maya Chen: another procurement note — we need a line-item for indemnity and export controls, will you accept procurement-standard language?
[00:05:17] Jordan Metz: we'll route legal — some language variations are ok; major indemnities around third-party content are negotiable.
[00:05:24] Renee Park: do you support PO payment nets 60? our standard is net 60 for vendors.
[00:05:29] Jordan Metz: Redwood standard is net 30 but enterprise customers can get net 60 with procurement approval; i'll flag for finance.
[00:05:35] Diego Alvarez: network egress — we have a corporate firewall tiering that charges a lot for cross-region egress. how much does redwood's regional routing reduce that?
[00:05:44] Priya Shah: if we route traffic to an EU cluster and keep ingress/egress internal, you only pay intra-region egress; cross-region falls back to standard internet egress. provide your topology and we'll map it.
[00:05:55] Alex Rivera: regarding SSO: we require SAML 2.0 with SCIM for group sync and role mapping; can Redwood integrate with our Okta instance?
[00:06:03] Priya Shah: yes, Okta via SAML + SCIM is standard. RBAC can be mapped to Okta groups; for Private we can also integrate with your AD via LDAP.
[00:06:12] Maya Chen: timeline — if legal signs MSA by 4/14 and we get perf numbers by 4/18, procurement can issue PO 4/21 and pilot can start 4/24, is that a realistic path?
[00:06:22] Jordan Metz: that's tight but doable. we'll prioritise the perf run and legal pack.
[00:06:27] Priya Shah: can i ask Diego for a small connectivity test? just a traceroute and sample token exchange to validate egress path.
[00:06:33] Diego Alvarez: yep, i'll take that as an action.
[00:06:36] Jordan Metz: quick pause — i'll share the MSA redline doc now in chat (link) and mark our suggested positions.
[00:06:44] Alex Rivera: there's a clause about subprocessor lists; we need a guaranteed 30 day notification for new subprocessors.
[00:06:50] Jordan Metz: doable. we can commit to notification windows in the DPA.
[00:06:54] Maya Chen: can you also include a sample cost model with a blended egress estimate? we need that for internal approval.
[00:07:00] Jordan Metz: yes — i'll include a 3-scenario cost model (pilot, steady-state, peak).
[00:07:06] Priya Shah: about SLA — is 99.95 in the MSA acceptable? if Helios needs 99.99 that usually pushes to Dedicated with replication guarantees.
[00:07:15] Alex Rivera: security prefers the higher SLA for customer-critical flows, but we can accept 99.95 for non-critical. can we carve the SLA by endpoint?
[00:07:24] Priya Shah: yes, per-route SLAs are supported; critical endpoints can be pinned to Dedicated nodes with higher SLOs.
[00:07:32] Renee Park: procurement will need an exhibit listing support SLAs, P1/P2 response times, and escalation matrix.
[00:07:39] Jordan Metz: we'll provide a support exhibit; Liam (CSM) will be primary contact for onboarding.
[00:07:45] Liam O'Connor: hi — happy to own that and coordinate the pilot runbook.
[00:07:48] Diego Alvarez: one more technical thing — how do you handle model upgrades? we need deterministic versioning for audits.
[00:07:55] Priya Shah: we allow model pinning per route and maintain version history; upgrades are via controlled rollouts with canary traffic and automatic rollback on regressions. we'll include the rollout policy doc.
[00:08:07] Alex Rivera: okay that's good.
[00:08:10] Jordan Metz: moving toward a recap — open items: annotated MSA/DPA, KMS decision (BYOK hosted vs Private), perf benchmark results, procurement PO timeline, Diego to share network topology, and Liam will send pilot runbook.
[00:08:25] Maya Chen: yes and pricing — need the blended egress estimate and commitment options.
[00:08:29] Jordan Metz: agreed. final Qs?
[00:08:33] Alex Rivera: small one — will logs contain full request/response or just metadata?
[00:08:38] Priya Shah: by default full metadata and hashed request/response are stored; storing full cleartext request/response is available under Private or with explicit DPA provisions.
[00:08:50] Renee Park: procurement note: please include W-9 and standard invoicing details with the MSA package.
[00:08:56] Jordan Metz: will do.
[00:09:00] Jordan Metz: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the documents and benchmarks. expect Jordan's MSA packet by Friday.
[00:09:07] Maya Chen: thanks.
[00:09:09] Alex Rivera: thanks, bye.
[00:09:11] [call continues — side-channel discussion, approvals and calendar scheduling — trimmed for brevity]
[00:45:10] Priya Shah: (later in the call) i ran the quick local sim — with BYOK hosted we saw p95 ~520ms, with Dedicated pre-warmed pools p95 ~310ms on similar model size. quantized variant reduced cost by ~28% with a small quality delta.
[00:46:02] Maya Chen: that p95 variance is useful; can you capture the exact test config?
[00:46:08] Priya Shah: yes, i'll attach the test matrix and raw logs to the perf report.
[00:50:15] Jordan Metz: to confirm next steps verbally: Jordan to send MSA/DPA annotated, Priya to run formal perf and attach configs, Diego to share topology, Renee to confirm PO timing, Liam to prepare onboarding runbook.
[00:50:30] Alex Rivera: one more ask — can Redwood provide a short threat model document for the BYOK hosted option? we need it for our review.
[00:50:38] Priya Shah: yes will provide a BYOK threat model and mitigations doc.
[00:50:45] Jordan Metz: great. we'll reconvene next week if legal needs clarity. thanks all.
[00:50:51] [END]
